'''Jingdong Zhang''' (June 2, 1968 – January 9, 2020) was a Chinese–Danish chemist and professor of chemistry at the [[Technical University of Denmark]]. Her research considered nanochemistry and the novel materials for catalysis, as well as the development of advanced characterisation techniques such as [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunnelling microscopy]] and [[atomic force microscopy]]. She was elected to the [[:da:Akademiet for de Tekniske Videnskaber|Akademiet for de Tekniske Videnskaber]] in 2017.

== Early life and education ==
Zhang was born in 1968 in [[China]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Jingdong Zhang (1968 – 2020) :: ChemViews Magazine :: ChemistryViews|url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/11212286/Jingdong_Zhang_1968__2020.html#:~:text=Jingdong%20Zhang,%20Professor%20of%20Chemistry,tunnelling%20and%20atomic%20force%20microscopy.|access-date=2021-04-05|website=www.chemistryviews.org| date=15 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> She studied chemistry and environmental engineering at [[Shanghai University]]. After earning her master's degree, Zhang moved to the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]' Changchun Institute of Applied Chemistry (CIAC) for her graduate research.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Engelbrekt|first1=Christian|last2=Mao|first2=Bingwei|last3=Ulstrup|first3=Jens|last4=Xiao|first4=Xinxin|date=2021|title=In Memoriam: Prof. Jingdong Zhang|url=https://chemistry-europe.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/celc.202100023|journal=ChemElectroChem|volume=8|issue=1|pages=257–259|doi=10.1002/celc.202100023|s2cid=234138891 |issn=2196-0216|doi-access=free}}</ref> Here she worked under the supervision of [[Erkang Wang]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Zhang was appointed to the [[Exploratory Research for Advanced Technology]] (ERATO) project, which saw her working on electrochemiscopy at the [[Kyushu University]] in [[Sendai]], Japan.<ref name=":0" /> She joined the faculty at the [[Technical University of Denmark]] in 1998, where she was eventually promoted to professor in 2016.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Profile - DTU Chemistry|url=https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Organic-Inorganic-Chemistry/NanoChemistry/Jingdong1/Profile|url-status=dead|access-date=2021-04-05|website=KEMI DTU|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114111643/https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Organic-Inorganic-Chemistry/NanoChemistry/Jingdong1/Profile}}</ref> Her research considered electrochemistry for nanomedicines and sustainable energy.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Research - DTU Chemistry|url=https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Organic-Inorganic-Chemistry/NanoChemistry/Jingdong1/Research|access-date=2021-04-05|website=KEMI DTU|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115214821/https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/research/organic-inorganic-chemistry/nanochemistry/jingdong1/research|url-status=dead}}</ref> In particular, she was interested in the electrochemistry that occurs at interfaces.<ref name=":2" /> During the late nineties, electrochemistry rapidly grew as a research area, integrating aspects of solid state physics and materials science. Zhang was quick to pick up new materials and characterisation techniques, including [[atomic force microscopy]] at single molecule resolution.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|title=In Memoriam: Prof. Jingdong Zhang: ChemElectroChem|url=https://chemistry-europe.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/toc/10.1002/(ISSN)2196-0216.Jingdong-Zhang|journal=Chemistry Europe|language=en|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)2196-0216|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She was particularly interested in redox metalloproteins and enzymes and new (bio)electrochemical surfaces.<ref name=":3" /> These surfaces included graphene, nanoparticles and nanoporous metallic surfaces.<ref name=":3" />

She was awarded the [[Danish Society of Engineers]] Agnes and Betzy Prize in 2011.<ref name=":1" /> The following year she was elected to the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]]. In 2017 Zhang was appointed to the [[:da:Akademiet for de Tekniske Videnskaber|Akademiet for de Tekniske Videnskaber]]. Zhang was a member of the editorial board of [[ChemElectroChem]]. A special issue of [[ChemElectroChem]] honouring Zhang and her legacy was published in 2021.<ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
Zhang was married to [[Qijin Chi]], a chemist at the [[Technical University of Denmark]], with whom she had one son.<ref name=":3" />
